items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates and permit only bounded reversible changes that preserve existing consent, disclosures, data handling, provenance, and claims boundaries. Evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication, least privilege, secrets handling, container isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS coverage. Compliance is technical evidence only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not proof of exploitation. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, medium for bounded reversible growth.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Use authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.
